candidates.exact_span: The percent solids of sewage sludge that contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 90% based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets an enforceable numeric solids limit (≥90%); different readings of the measurement basis ('prior to mixing with other materials') or whether the sludge qualifies as containing unstabilized primary solids would change which limit applies and whether a reported solids value exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or an anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines whether Alternative 8's 90% solids limit is triggered; divergent interpretations of prior aerobic/anaerobic treatment would change limit applicability and compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: No significant amount of the sewage sludge shall be present on the land surface within one hour after the sewage sludge is injected.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a time-bound surface-presence standard with the qualifier 'significant amount'; different interpretations of what constitutes a significant surface amount or the one-hour window would change whether an observed condition is treated as exceeding an applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: When sewage sludge that is injected below the surface of the land is Class A with respect to pathogens, the sewage sludge shall be injected below the land surface within eight hours after being discharged from the pathogen treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates an eight-hour injection timing requirement conditioned on Class A pathogen status; interpretation of Class A classification, discharge time from pathogen treatment, and injection timing could change enforceable limit applicability (A) and whether related monitoring or missing-data periods are required or satisfiable (B, C).

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge applied to the land surface or placed on a surface disposal site shall be incorporated into the soil within six hours after application to or placement on the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a six-hour incorporation timing standard; different interpretations of application/placement time or incorporation completion would change whether a reported or observed condition exceeds the applicable requirement.

candidates.exact_span: When sewage sludge that is incorporated into the soil is Class A with respect to pathogens, the sewage sludge shall be applied to or placed on the land within eight hours after being discharged from the pathogen treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates an eight-hour land-application timing requirement for Class A sludge; interpretation of Class A status, pathogen-treatment discharge time, and application timing could change limit applicability (A) and associated monitoring or missing-evidence classification (B, C).

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit shall be covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a daily cover requirement tied to 'active sewage sludge unit' and 'operating day'; different readings of those terms or of what satisfies 'covered' would change whether a facility is judged to meet the operative standard.

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, 5. Methane Gas Control Within a Structure On Site
candidates.exact_span: When cover is placed on an active surface disposal site, the methane gas concentration in the air in any structure shall not exceed 25% of the lower ex plosive limit (LEL) for methane gas during the period that the disposal site is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric methane ceiling (25% of LEL) conditioned on cover placement and site activity; interpretation of when the site is active, which structures are covered, and how LEL is applied would change limit selection (A) and whether continuous structure monitoring is in scope (B).

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, 6. Methane Gas Control at Property Line
candidates.exact_span: The concentration of methane gas in air at the property line of the surface disposal site shall not exceed the LEL for methane gas during the period that the disposal site is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a property-line methane limit at 100% LEL while the site is active; different interpretations of site activity period or LEL measurement basis would change applicable limit comparisons (A) and continuous property-line monitoring obligations (B).

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, D. Monitoring Requirements
candidates.exact_span: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) Test - Once/Permit Life, performed within one year from the effective date of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines a permit-life TCLP monitoring obligation with a one-year startup window; interpretation of permit effective date, permit life, and whether the test was due would change required-monitoring determinations (B) and how absent TCLP results are classified (C).

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, D. Monitoring Requirements
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies annual PCB monitoring frequency; whether this requirement applies to a given facility or period would change monitoring-obligation computations.

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, D. Monitoring Requirements
candidates.exact_span: Methane Gas in covered structures on site - Continuous
candidates.computation_change_reason: Mandates continuous methane monitoring in covered on-site structures; interpretation of which structures qualify as covered and when continuous monitoring is required would change monitoring-obligation results (B) and classification of missing continuous data (C).

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, D. Monitoring Requirements
candidates.exact_span: Methane Gas at property line - Continuous
candidates.computation_change_reason: Mandates continuous property-line methane monitoring while applicable; different readings of site activity or monitoring location would change obligation applicability (B) and how gaps in continuous records are treated (C).

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, D. Monitoring Requirements, sludge-amount table
candidates.exact_span: All other pollutants shall be monitored at the frequency shown below:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scopes residual pollutant monitoring to the tiered schedule that follows; interpretation of which pollutants fall under 'all other pollutants' would change which monitoring frequencies are assigned.

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, D. Monitoring Requirements, sludge-amount table, row 0 ≤ Sludge < 290
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigns annual monitoring for facilities below 290 metric tons of sludge per 365-day period; interpretation of sludge tonnage calculation or period boundaries would change required frequency (B) and whether missing annual results indicate required-but-unreported monitoring (C).

candidates.locator: page 18, section part_i, D. Monitoring Requirements, sludge-amount table, row 290 ≤ Sludge < 1,500
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigns quarterly monitoring for mid-tier sludge volumes; different readings of the 290–1,500 metric-ton threshold or rolling 365-day sludge total would change required monitoring frequency (B) and missing-data semantics for expected quarterly results (C).
